AI and ML.blurb: Rust in machine learning and AI infrastructure: inference runtimes, tensor libraries, Python bindings and model serving.

AI-Assisted Coding.blurb: Coding agents and LLMs writing, porting and reviewing Rust: what works, what breaks and why the compiler matters here.

Async.blurb: Futures, executors and async/await in Rust: Tokio, smol, async closures and what changes as the language catches up.

CLI Tools.blurb: Command-line tools written in Rust, and how to build your own: ripgrep, uv, clap and friends.

Community.blurb: The people side of Rust: the Rust Foundation, conferences, surveys, governance, jobs and the projects maintainers keep alive.

Compiler.blurb: rustc and what sits under it: compile times, codegen backends, linkers, the parallel front end and compiler internals.

Databases.blurb: Databases written in Rust and the crates to talk to them: Diesel, SQLx, SeaORM, embedded stores and data engines.

Embedded.blurb: Rust on microcontrollers and hardware: embedded HALs, no_std, drones, automotive and the boards people ship with it.

GUI and Desktop.blurb: Desktop and GUI apps in Rust: Tauri, egui, Slint, GPUI, Iced and terminal UIs, plus the state of the ecosystem.

Game Development.blurb: Games and engines in Rust: Bevy, Fyrox, emulators, simulations and what people ship with them.

Interop.blurb: Rust next to other languages: C and C++ FFI, PyO3 and Python bindings, Zig, Go and gradual migration.

Language Features.blurb: New and upcoming language features: releases, editions, RFCs, stabilizations, traits, macros and error handling.

Learning Rust.blurb: Getting good at Rust: books, courses, exercises, project ideas, idioms and how long it really takes.

Memory Safety.blurb: What Rust's ownership model prevents and where unsafe comes in: comparisons with C and C++, CVEs and government guidance.

Networking.blurb: Network software in Rust: proxies, DNS, HTTP stacks, QUIC and the services that carry real traffic.

Operating Systems.blurb: Operating systems and system software in Rust beyond the Linux kernel: systemd, Redox, Windows, Android and hobby OS projects.

Performance.blurb: Making Rust fast and measuring it: benchmarks, profiling, allocation, SIMD and binary size.

Rewrites.blurb: Existing software rewritten in Rust: coreutils, bzip2, linkers, runtimes and the debate about when a rewrite is worth it.

Rust in Production.blurb: Companies running Rust for real: Microsoft, Google, AWS, Cloudflare, Meta and smaller teams, with what they gained and what it cost.

Safety-Critical.blurb: Rust where failure is not an option: automotive, aerospace, medical, Ferrocene, certification and the language specification.

Security.blurb: Security work in and with Rust: supply-chain attacks on crates, vulnerability reports, fuzzing and security tools written in Rust.

Tooling.blurb: The tools around the language: Cargo, Clippy, rust-analyzer, debuggers, Miri, linters and editor setups.

Web Development.blurb: Backends, frontends and full-stack Rust: Axum, Actix, Leptos, Dioxus, static sites and the APIs people build with them.

WebAssembly.blurb: Rust compiled to WebAssembly: in the browser, on the edge and as a plugin format, plus the tooling around it.
